title: Carrot Cake
subtitle: Moist spiced carrot cake with cream cheese frosting
excerpt: A deeply moist, warmly spiced cake packed with grated carrot and walnuts, topped with a thick cream cheese frosting. The most popular modern British cake.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carrot cake is one of those dishes where the national origin is disputed and the history is layered. Carrots have been used to sweeten cakes since at least the medieval period, when sugar was expensive and root vegetables were the practical substitute. A form of carrot pudding appears in the seventeenth century. The modern carrot cake, with its oil-based batter, grated fresh carrot, spice, and cream cheese frosting, emerged in American and British recipe books during the second half of the twentieth century and became one of the most popular cakes sold in British coffee shops and bakeries from the 1980s onwards. The oil rather than butter in the batter is what produces the characteristic very moist crumb: oil does not solidify at room temperature as butter does, so the cake stays soft even when cold. The cream cheese frosting should be firmly whipped: if the cream cheese is too soft or the icing sugar is added too quickly, the frosting will be liquid rather than spreadable.

recipeTools.notes: Two 20 cm round sandwich tins or one deep 20 cm cake tin, greased and lined.

content.text: Grate the carrots on the large holes of a box grater and squeeze lightly to remove excess moisture before adding to the batter. Too much moisture from the carrots can make the centre of the cake sink. The batter comes together quickly because there is no creaming step: simply whisk the eggs, sugar, and oil together, then fold in the dry ingredients and grated carrot. Do not over-mix once the flour is added.

items.preparation: grated on the large side of a box grater, about 3 large carrots
roughly chopped, plus extra to decorate

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line two 20 cm sandwich tins. Whisk the eggs, both sugars, and oil together for 2 minutes. Sift in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder, cinnamon, mixed spice, and salt. Fold to combine. Fold in the grated carrot and walnuts.
Divide the batter between the tins. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely before frosting.

Make the frosting: beat the butter until pale, then beat in the cream cheese. Add the icing sugar gradually and the vanilla. Beat until smooth and firm. Spread one-third over the first sponge, sandwich the second on top, and spread the rest over the top and sides. Decorate with walnuts.
